Our Story – Z. Hinchliffe & Sons. Skip to content. Z. Hinchliffe & Sons. Producing Quality Cashmere Since 1766. Our Story. The business was founded by Zaccheus, (the 7 th Hinchliffe son) in 1766 as a trading company and in 1850, he built his company head-quarters in the rural, picturesque Yorkshire village of Denby Dale, and it remains in the very same place to this day. Denby Dale is situated in a natural valley, and our factory stands at the bottom in the shadow of the impressive Victorian railway viaduct that dominates the village. It was in fact Zaccheus Hinchliffe who laid the first stone when the viaduct was changed from its original wooden structure to stone in 1877, so important was this business man to the area. Of course, the railway and good road links were just two of the reasons why Zaccheus chose this location for his factory. Another major reason was the river Dearne, meandering through the valley. Water was collected from the river and held in a dam where it was then used as required for the dyeing and scouring involved with yarn spinning. This process carries on today. We use the naturally soft water of this Yorkshire area before it is treated and returned to the river, just as clean and pure as it was before. Being a sustainable business is becoming increasingly important to us and to our customers. None of our processes use azo dyes, formaldehyde, carcinogenic, hazardous or allergy inducing products, and we are striving to decrease our carbon footprint and reduce our energy consumption. Over the decades, many other businesses, such as clay pipe manufacturers, and other textile mills, grew up in Denby Dale, and the village started to expand. With the demand for a workforce, Z. Hinchliffe built several rows of houses to accommodate their factory workers as they moved in to the area. Other parcels of land were purchased and some was given over for the community, such as Denby Dale cricket field, which is played on every weekend during the summer months. Z. Hinchliffes being the largest employer in the village has had some influence on various community projects and is proud to have been associated with many of the infamous Denby Dale pies when in every generation the largest pie in the world is produced. Hartcliffe Mills – 2019. We combine the expertise built up through the generations with modern technological advances to produce the finest quality yarns in the international market. Graham Wilby. To this day the company is 100% privately owned still predominantly by the Hinchliffe family. Over the centuries many things have changed and evolved however the companies core values remain the same; The spinning of the finest natural raw materials into the highest quality yarns. Collections – Z. Hinchliffe & Sons. Skip to content. Z. Hinchliffe & Sons. Producing Quality Cashmere Since 1766. Collections. We offer various stock service collections which eliminates the requirement for minimum order quantities. However we are also able to produce any customer’s own shades in all our qualities. LAMBSWOOL. Most of our Lambswool, is shipped from Australia, and comes from the Merino breed of sheep. Merinos’ have been specially bred to produce the softest and finest wool. Lambswool is wool from the first shearing of the animal. We also have a new range of lambswool which is 100% sourced from Great Britain. The UK has over 60 breeds of sheep, all with different fibre lengths, textures and widths, so it took a while and many trials for us to find the right one to produce the best yarn for our customers. Using home grown wool is a new challenge but as it greatly reduces our carbon footprint it is important we persevere while it also benefits local farmers and the environment. WHY WOOL? Wool can be recycled; it is compostable, biodegradable and naturally renewable, making it friendly to the environment. It makes a fabric that can breathe, is elastic, gives natural odour control, warms us when we are cold and cools us when we overheat. Wool is also naturally fire retardant. These qualities give wool a wide and diverse range of uses. 2/17NM LAMBSWOOL. RANGE: 120 STOCK SERVICE SHADES. Our superior 2/17nm 100% merino lambswool is a very soft but durable yarn. Throughout production, we take our utmost care to protect our raw materials at every stage in order to create the best finished product we can. Our pallet of 120 shades includes solids, subtle mixtures and multi-coloured mixtures. It is refreshed with the new seasons shades every June. A machine washable finish can also be applied to the garment made from this yarn without any detrement to the shade and colour fastness. 1/15NM HARTCLIFFE LAMBSWOOL WEAVING RANGE. RANGE: 58 STOCK SERVICE SHADES. Our Hartcliffe range is made with 100% lambswool and has extra twist to give extra strength for the weaving trade. It produces a fine soft, durable, top quality cloth. Cashmere. 2/28NM CASHMERE. RANGE: 160 STOCK SERVICE SHADES. Our 2/28nm cashmere yarn has the finest handle, with a silky softness that can only be achieved by having a carefully controlled environment, as the finest fibre is teased into a yarn. Great care is taken so we do not lose any of the amazing natural handle that only cashmere can give. It produces a light garment, which looks refined but still gives warmth and comfort. Some people are surprised to learn that the Scottish cashmere story starts with goats. Not Scottish goats, but a hardy, mountain-dwelling breed that has adapted to the harsh environments and extreme temperatures of the Gobi Desert. To survive, the goats develop wonderfully thick coats made up of a coarse outer guard hair and a fine, soft undercoat. We use only the finest fibre – the white, downy undercoat that runs from the throat to belly. This yields a tiny amount: it takes fibre from one goat to knit a scarf, three to make a sweater. Traditionally, farmers would collect cashmere fibre by ceremonially combing their goats in the spring. Combing is still widely used today, alongside some farmers who prefer shearing. Nothing compares to Scottish cashmere. The way it looks, how it feels, the way it drapes. Created to Last. Scottish-spun cashmere is world-renowned. The ‘Scottish handle’ is more robust off the shelf, but soon blossoms. Cashmere knitwear is a wardrobe staple, as comfortable to wear on a summer afternoon as it is on a frosty winter morning. Scottish cashmere is appreciated by young and old – often passing from one generation. to the next. However, the longevity of cashmere isn’t a given. The processes involved in creating cashmere yarn play a big part. We’ve refined our traditional techniques over two centuries to create a cashmere yarn that pills less than any other. Responsible Sources. Cashmere. goats are usually tended by nomadic cashmere farmers; a typical. farmer will often have a flock of 2-300. It’s. easy to see why animal welfare, sustainability and traceability are. the three pillars of the cashmere industry’s ethical sourcing. initiatives. Working in partnership with our approved de-hairers, we encourage sustainable herding and. grazing practices, promote high standards of animal welfare, and work to protect this traditional way of life within nomadic communities.

We strive to deliver the purest knitwear experience, which is why we shun man-made fibres, instead using only 100% natural fibre yarns in the production of our knitwear. ____. We trawl the globe in search of the most prestigious spinners to ensure every piece of Paul James knitwear is crafted from the most luxurious materials. We travel to Italy for extra-fine merino wool - then to Peru for a chunkier version – India and Egypt for premium cotton, South America for ultra warm, soft Alpaca and the British Isles for its famed wool and lambswool. We take these yarns and knit them into stylish, functional garments that are made to last. ____. RHYTHM TO CRAFT. A short film shot at our Leicestershire factory. OUR ETHOS. Our decades of knowledge, skill and craftsmanship combine seamlessly with the latest machinery and traditional manufacturing techniques, meaning we can design and fashion exclusively crafted knitwear, for a price that’s fair. Moreover, our sweaters are natural and sustainable, thus reducing our reliance on man-made fibres in our clothing. Our Designs. Our collections make the everyday extraordinary. We craft timeless classics and wardrobe staples from the finest alpaca, cotton, cashmere, merino wool and Lambswool, each piece a faultless combination of form and function. We champion ethically sourced products and the wonders of British design and manufacturing in equal measure. Our Yarns. At Paul James we use only 100% natural yarns. Evolved over thousands of years, our yarns are nature’s performance fabrics. Our fibres are skin friendly, breathable, offer outstanding wicking and thermoregulating properties, sustainable, beautiful in colour and handle but most importantly of all, really comfortable to wear. Our Factories. We knit, sew, wash, steam and press over 95 percent of our products in our own factories. This means that we are in control of the entire process, with no middlemen. Our yarns are spun by our carefully handpicked spinners, crafted by our teams all across the world, then delivered directly to our customers. By working in this methodical pattern, we can be sure of the integrity of our clothing and keep our prices fair and just for the quality of the materials used. Our Vision. Having learnt about the fashion industry from the factory floor up, with a clear understanding of the transient nature of a customer's’ relationship with brands and trends, we focus only on creating the most accessible, luxury interpretations of timeless wardrobe staples, built to last longer than any trend. Love Cashmere is a Scottish cashmere knitwear brand designed, crafted and finished in our own mill in Hawick, the historic home of fine cashmere. For over 35 years, we have been dedicated to the art of knitwear manufacturing, producing world-class cashmere for some of the world’s most respected designer brands. Inside our Hawick mill. Today, we bring that same expertise directly to our own collection, combining heritage skills, modern design and exceptional value. Every Love Cashmere garment is thoughtfully designed in-house, then carefully knitted and hand-finished by highly skilled craftsmen and women whose knowledge has been passed down through generations. This continuity of skill, paired with advanced knitting technology, allows us to create beautifully refined cashmere with clarity, strength and exceptional softness, designed to last and improve with wear. Our philosophy is simple: to offer authentic Scottish cashmere of uncompromising quality at an accessible luxury price. By designing, manufacturing and selling directly from our mill, we remove unnecessary mark-ups and deliver true cashmere luxury without compromise. The source of our luxury cashmere. The Love Cashmere label represents the finest Scottish craftsmanship. Our cashmere begins its journey far from Scotland, using ultra-fine fibres sourced from sustainably managed herds in Inner Mongolia, where Capra hircus goats endure winter temperatures of up to minus forty degrees Celsius. It is this harsh natural environment that produces the precious, ultra-soft undercoat that defines true cashmere. From fibre to finished yarn. To survive, the goats develop a dual coat consisting of a coarse outer guard hair and a fine, downy underlayer. We use only the finest fibre, the white, soft undercoat found primarily along the throat and belly. Remarkably rare, the yield is extremely small. The fibre from a single goat is enough to knit just one scarf, while around three goats are required to produce a sweater. Traditionally, cashmere is collected in spring by gently combing the goats as they naturally shed their winter coats. This practice is still widely used today alongside selective shearing. Once collected, the fibre is dyed, carded and spun using Scotland’s famously soft water, a critical element in achieving the clarity, softness and durability for which Scottish cashmere is renowned. We work exclusively with the world’s most respected yarn spinners, including Cariaggi and Todd & Duncan, ensuring every piece begins with exceptional raw materials. Celebrated worldwide, Scottish cashmere is valued not only for its unrivalled softness, but also for its strength, longevity and ability to retain its beauty over time. These qualities sit at the heart of every Love Cashmere piece. Responsibly sourced. Our cashmere is responsibly sourced from trusted suppliers who prioritise animal welfare, traceability and long-term land stewardship. The majority of the fibre used in our yarns is certified by the Sustainable Fibre Alliance (SFA), supporting responsible sourcing and improved livelihoods for herding communities. Our approach to responsible manufacturing. All manufacturing is carried out in our Scottish mill using low-impact processes, careful water management and minimal waste. By producing in small batches and maintaining a short, transparent supply chain, we reduce unnecessary transport and ensure each piece reflects a considered, sustainable approach to luxury cashmere. Cashmere is our craft. Cashmere is not just what we do, it is our craft and our heritage. Scotland remains one of the world’s few true centres of excellence for luxury knitwear, and at Love Cashmere we are proud to carry that tradition forward, creating timeless designs intended to be worn, treasured and passed on. The craft behind each garment. Made in our Scottish mill using time-honoured techniques, every garment reflects generations of expertise, care and attention to detail. About Us NEW. – Scottish Cashmere Collection. Skip to content. Log in. Log in. Cart. Item added to your cart. View cart. About Us. We are a small family business based in Hawick, in the Scottish Borders (the home of Scottish Knitwear), with over 40 years experience in the knitwear industry making gloves and scarves to a high standard. After retiring and selling his previous knitwear business my dad decided to set up a small craft business specialising in handcrafted cashmere accessories made by him and other small local producers and I joined after a career change in 2019. We get our yarn in very small batches which allows us to keep our prices competitively low but also means we have a large range of colours that change regularly. We normally have over 50 yarns available, so if you are looking for a specific colour and can’t see it in our online store please get in touch. We may have it in stock already, or may have yarn to allow us to make it for you. “Hoyk and the Hosiery”: A short history of Hawick’s knitwear industry. Set where the Slitrig meets the River Teviot, Hawick grew from a Borders market town into one of Britain’s great textile centres. For more than two centuries its mills and workshops have turned fine yarns into world-class knitwear—especially cashmere—giving the town a reputation that still resonates far beyond Scotland. Stockings and the first frames (18th century). Although hand-knitting was already common, Hawick’s organised hosiery trade traditionally dates to 1771, when Bailie John Hardie introduced the first stocking frames to the town. Within twenty years the number of frames had multiplied, and knitters began to specialise in fine-gauge stockings and hose. Water from the Teviot and Slitrig powered early mills; later, steam and electricity took over as the industry scaled. Power, transport and new materials (19th century). Hawick’s location and rivers made it ideal for mechanised production, and the arrival of the railway in the 1840s opened export routes south and overseas. Crucially, the de-hairing and separation techniques popularised in the 19th century made cashmere viable at scale, laying the groundwork for Hawick’s long association with luxury knitwear. By the late 1800s the town was recognised internationally for high-quality knitted goods. The makers who shaped the town. Several storied companies took root in Hawick and helped define the town’s identity: Pringle of Scotland (1815) started with hosiery and underwear before becoming a fashion name; its archives trace the broader Hawick story. Lyle & Scott (1874) began in Hawick and later became synonymous with knitwear on the golf course. William Lockie (1874) remains one of the oldest family-run knitwear makers in town. Peter Scott (1878) built a reputation for luxury knitwear from its Buccleuch Street works. Hawick Hosiery Company / Hawico (from 1874) still produces at its original Duke Street mill. Johnstons of Elgin (founded 1797) expanded into knitting at Hawick’s Eastfield Mill, making the town a key site in a vertically-integrated Scottish luxury business. Barrie (1903) became a vital luxury supplier; its acquisition by Chanel in 2012 underlined Hawick’s place in top-tier fashion supply chains. Design turns fashion (early–mid 20th century). Technical “fully-fashioned” knitting—shaping panels to the body on the machine—helped Hawick makers move beyond underwear into outerwear. At Pringle, designer Otto Weisz (appointed 1934) popularised the twinset and developed argyle for knitwear, styles that travelled from Scotland to Hollywood and into everyday wardrobe. Boom, shocks and resilience (late 20th–early 21st century). Post-war decades were prosperous; local sources even note Hawick as one of the UK’s highest-earning towns per head in the 1960s. Globalisation then bit hard: some production moved abroad, and famous factories closed—the Pringle plant in Hawick shuttered in 2008; Hawick Knitwear went into administration in 2016; Peter Scott ceased production that same year. Yet the town also saw lifelines and reinvention: Chanel’s rescue of Barrie (2012) safeguarded skilled jobs and investment, and specialist makers doubled down on premium natural fibres and craftsmanship. What endures today. Walk the riverside and you’ll still see mill buildings—like Tower Mill, a rare bridge-built textile mill with a Victorian waterwheel—now repurposed but emblematic of how water power seeded the industry. The Borders Textile Towerhouse museum tells the story from hosiery to high fashion. Meanwhile, Hawick makers continue to supply leading houses and expand with new technology: Johnstons’ Hawick site runs advanced Shima Seiki knitting, and recent investment has increased capacity to meet global demand for Scottish Cashmere. Why Hawick still matters. Hawick’s edge has always been a blend of know-how, water and yarn: generations of frame- and machine-knitters who can coax impeccable handle from the soft Borders water and the world’s best fibres. Even after closures and consolidation, that ecosystem of skills keeps the town’s “made in Hawick” label meaningful—rooted in place, but connected to fashion capitals everywhere,. pages.text: Zian Hi-Tech & Yunshang Cashmere. Skip to content. Contact us. Zian Hi-Tech · Yunshang Cashmere. The leading supply chain for sustainability-certified, high-quality cashmere fibre. For over 20 years, Zian Hi-Tech and Yunshang Cashmere have been recognised as a leading supply chain for the highest quality dehaired Chinese cashmere fibre and combed cashmere top, serving many illustrious European spinning and weaving mills. Our unique advantage comes from vertical control of the entire cashmere production chain and our firmly set principles, which allow sustainability improvements to be adopted rapidly. Today, we hold an outstanding reputation for the consistent quality of our fibre, our expertise in sustainable cashmere production practices, and the transparency of our service. Talk to us. Our certifications. Supplying the world's leading mills and brands since 1998. Founded. since 1998. Finest fibre. down to 14.5 µm. Combed top length. up to 50 mm. Coarse hair content. as low as <0.005 %. Who we are. Two companies, one cashmere supply chain. Zian Hi-Tech and Yunshang Cashmere work together so that the same team is accountable for your fibre from the herd to delivery. UK & Europe commercial arm · Since 1998. Zian Hi-Tech (U.K.) Limited. Our commercial arm for the UK and Europe, working directly with brands and European spinning and weaving mills on sales, partnerships, sustainability and service. Chinese production arm · Since 2009. Yunshang Cashmere (Xi'an) Co., Ltd. Our production company in Xi'an, sourcing raw cashmere from Inner Mongolia and processing it in our own dehairing plant into dehaired fibre and cashmere top. World's first Regenerative Organic Certified® cashmere supplier. Yunshang Cashmere. Founded in 2009, Yunshang Cashmere has earned a strong reputation in the high-end fashion and textile industry as a trusted supplier of premium cashmere fibre. Our success is built on consistency, reliability and innovation. By building close relationships with every stakeholder in the supply chain, from farmers to designers, we turn our customers' goals into tangible results. This integrated approach has made Yunshang one of the first certified organic cashmere suppliers in the industry and, more recently, the world's first Regenerative Organic Certified® cashmere supplier. Where our cashmere comes from. The grasslands of Inner Mongolia. Each spring, Yunshang sources raw cashmere from independent goat farmers in two regions of Inner Mongolia: Alashan and Erdos. The raw fibre then travels to our own dehairing plant in Xi'an. Every herd is assigned a unique ID, so each bale stays traceable to the farm it came from. Simplified map; boundaries approximate. Our sustainability. Sustainability is our leading principle. We are keen to share the actions that drive us towards it. 01. Animal welfare. We enforce an animal welfare code that our farmer suppliers must follow, so goats are bred, raised and combed in a cruelty-free way. We also work with local government and Chinese NGOs to protect goat herds and herdsmen during extreme weather. 02. Preserving the environment. Our farmers' goat herds graze freely across between 2.7 and 6.7 km² of grassland each. 03. Staff wellbeing. Yunshang is a Fair Wage certified employer. Every staff member is offered a full pension, free accommodation for themselves and their families, three free meals a day, free utilities, and a garden and outdoor exercise area. 04. Full traceability. Each cashmere herd is assigned a unique ID, and traceability is recorded throughout production, so we can always identify the individual farm our material comes from. Our certification journey. Each step independently audited, and often a first for the cashmere industry. 2020. SFA. Certified to the Sustainable Fibre Alliance Cashmere Standard. 2022. GOTS. Certified to the Global Organic Textile Standard. 2023. Fair for Life. Certified for fair trade and responsible supply chains. 2024. Regenerative Organic Certified®. Certified for soil health, animal welfare and social fairness. 2025. Textile Exchange LCA. Helped collect primary data for the first comprehensive life cycle assessment of cashmere. 2026. Fair Wage & emissions data. Fair Wage certified, and collecting emissions data across our farm and factory supply chain. We supply cashmere certified to SFA, GOTS, Fair for Life and Regenerative Organic standards, depending on origin and grade, and Yunshang is a Fair Wage certified employer. Verify each one on the certifier's own register: Sustainable Fibre Alliance. Animal welfare, rangeland health and responsible processing. sustainablefibre.org. Global Organic Textile Standard. Organic and ecological textiles, certified through Ecocert. View certificate. Fair for Life. Fair trade and responsible supply chains. View certificate. Regenerative Organic Certified®. Certified by the Regenerative Organic Alliance. View certificate. Fair Wage Certified. Fair Wage Network, valid 15 March 2026 to 15 March 2027. View certificate (PDF). Our product. Dehaired cashmere fibre and cashmere top. Only the highest quality, sustainable cashmere, sourced from Alashan and Erdos in Inner Mongolia. Fibre diameter. Down to 14.5 µm — we supply and process fibre as fine as 14.5 microns. Fibre length. Up to 44 mm dehaired · 50 mm combed top — dehaired fibre up to 44 millimetres and combed cashmere top up to 50 millimetres long. Coarse hair content. As low as <0.005% — exceptionally clean dehairing for a softer, purer fibre. Colour quality. White for white — no black or dark fibres and a maximum of 6 fawn fibres per 5 grams of cashmere, with whiteness above 70%. What is dehairing? Raw cashmere arrives mixed with the goat's coarse outer guard hair, grease and other contaminants. Dehairing removes them, leaving only the fine, soft undercoat that is spun into yarn and woven into fabric. For cashmere top, we then comb the dehaired fibre to a uniform length and fineness, ready for spinning mills to make worsted yarn, or for weavers to make worsted fabric. Our production. A vertically integrated supply chain, built over two decades. From raw fibre to delivery, every stage happens at our own plant in Xi'an. Raw fibre sorting First sort. Washing & scouring Removing grease and dirt. Clean fibre sorting Second sort & contaminant removal. Dehairing & carding Separating the fine undercoat. Combing Cashmere top only. Packaging & delivery Tested before shipping. Tested three ways. We take random samples at every stage of production and test them in our in-house lab for fineness, length, colour and contamination. Results are compared with like-for-like tests at our customers' own labs and at independent third-party laboratories, and we ship only once every party's requirements are met. Our site in Xi'an. Our 39,960 m² site brings production together with staff dormitories, a canteen and a garden for our team. Commercial and production, together. Zian Hi-Tech in the UK and Europe and Yunshang Cashmere in Xi'an work as one team, so quality, traceability and service are managed end to end. Our team. Talk to the people behind the fibre.
